# Downloading from ENA instead {#sec-ena}

Because ENA mirrors SRA ([The databases](databases.qmd)), most runs are also
available from ENA as ready-made, gzipped FASTQ files **with MD5 checksums**.
No SRA Toolkit, no conversion, no temporary space. It's often the simplest
option.

| | SRA Toolkit | ENA |
|---|---|---|
| Software | prefetch + fasterq-dump | `wget` / `curl` |
| Temp space | 10–20× the `.sra` | none |
| Output | uncompressed FASTQ, needs gzip | `.fastq.gz` |
| Checksums | `vdb-validate` | MD5 per file |
| Read names | `SRR....N` | `SRR....N` (similar) |
| Availability | every SRA run | most runs; a few very new or unusual ones lack FASTQ |

## Step by step

1. Get the file list:

   ```bash
   curl -s "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=SRR1039508&result=read_run&fields=run_accession,fastq_ftp,fastq_md5,fastq_bytes&format=tsv"
   ```

   ```
   run_accession  fastq_ftp                                                           fastq_md5          fastq_bytes
   SRR1039508     ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz;ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_2.fastq.gz   <md5_1>;<md5_2>   1243786980;1230997455
   ```

   `fastq_ftp` and `fastq_md5` hold one entry per file, separated by `;`.
   The `accession` can be a run, a sample, an experiment or a whole project
   (`PRJNA229998`, `SRP033351`).

2. Download (the links work over HTTPS or FTP):

   ```bash
   wget -c https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR103/008/SRR1039508/SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz
   ```

   `-c` resumes an interrupted download.

3. Check against the MD5s:

   ```bash
   echo "<md5_1>  SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz" | md5sum -c
   ```

[`scripts/ena_download.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/ena_download.sh)
does all three for every run of an accession:

```bash
bash scripts/ena_download.sh PRJNA229998 fastq
```

It downloads **every** file ENA lists for that accession (including orphan-read
files), so for a subset, run it per run accession, e.g. in a loop over
`SRR_Acc_List.txt`.

::: {.callout-note}
For very large downloads, ENA also supports Aspera and the
[ENA File Downloader](https://github.com/enasequence/enaBrowserTools)
tools, which are faster than `wget` over long distances.
:::
